citation.authors: Bączek KK, Leng Cheng S, Amanda G, Achaiah A et al

record.population: 1,071 adults with confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis in the British Thoracic Society ILD Registry, 2013 to 2024 (ethnicity recorded for 918: 55.4% white, 14.2% non-white including Black, South Asian and mixed)
record.design: Retrospective registry study with multivariable logistic regression
record.finding: Non-white patients presented younger (52 against 54 years) with more breathlessness (46% against 33%) and cough (44% against 27%), more CT nodularity (54% against 36%) and abnormal liver tests (16% against 9%), and more comorbidity. Lung physiology was comparable. Immunosuppression was more likely with non-white ethnicity (odds ratio 3.20) and male sex (2.34). The authors say treatment decisions were more influenced by sex and ethnicity than by lung function or imaging.
record.note: UK registry; non-white is a pooled group, so Black adults alone are not separated in the abstract. Abstract read.
